question:
The weight of an object was 60 N when measured on the surface of the earth.

What would be its weight when measured on the surface of the moon?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The weight of an object is the force exerted on it due to gravity.
 
• On the moon, the gravitational force is about 1/6th that of the earth.
 
• If an object weighs 60 N on the earth, it will weigh approximately 10 N on the moon.
 
• This is because the gravitational acceleration on the moon is about 1.63 m/s² compared to 9.81 m/s² on the earth.

• **Weight vs. Mass**
 
 
• Weight is a force and depends on gravitational acceleration.
 
• Mass is a measure of the amount of matter in an object and is constant regardless of location.
 
 
 
• **Gravity on Other Celestial Bodies**
 
 
• Different celestial bodies have different gravitational accelerations.
 
• Mars has about 0.38 times the gravitational force of Earth.
 
• Jupiter has about 2.4 times the gravitational force of Earth.
 
 
 
• **Implications of Reduced Gravity**
 
 
• Reduced gravity affects human physiology, causing muscle atrophy and bone loss over time.
 
• Astronauts exercise in space to mitigate these effects.
